record.paper_title: Hadronic production of η–mesons: recent results and open questions
record.original_question: Why can the imaginary part of the eta-helium-3 scattering length be compatible with zero even though the pi-nucleon to eta-nucleon channel couples significantly near threshold and might suggest an imaginary part of order at least one fermi? The proposed resolution to assess is whether Pauli-principle blocking of the pi-NN intermediate state suppresses the most prominent inelastic channel in eta-deuteron and, to some extent, eta-helium-3 systems.

evidence.quote: One might therefore expect an imaginary part of the scattering length of the order of at least one fermi.
In contrast to this in a recent analysis of the world data base for η3He values for the imaginary part of the η3He scattering length were extracted that were compatible with zero [43].
Can we understand such a small imaginary part of the scattering length? The answer is yes.
As a consequence the potentially most prominent inelastic channel is blocked.
As the deuteron is a prominent building block also of 3He this argument at least to some extend should hold as well.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider the low-energy elastic scattering of an η-meson on a ³He nucleus, characterized by a complex scattering length a(η³He) = Re a + i Im a. Near threshold the η-nucleon system couples strongly to the πN channel, and on naive grounds one would expect that this strong coupling, propagated through πNN intermediate states inside the nucleus, would force Im a(η³He) to be of order at least 1 fm. Empirical analyses of near-threshold η³He production data, however, are compatible with Im a(η³He) ≈ 0.\n\nAssess the following proposed resolution: the antisymmetrization of the two-nucleon final state in the dominant inelastic intermediate channel ηNN → πNN forces the πNN system into quantum numbers that are largely forbidden by the Pauli principle near threshold, so that this otherwise prominent inelastic channel is strongly suppressed in η-deuteron and (to a lesser extent) η-³He systems. Show, within a coupled-channel few-body framework for the η-³He system, that Pauli blocking of the πNN intermediate state suppresses Im a(η³He) sufficiently to render it consistent with zero, and quantify the residual contribution from channels not affected by this blocking.
artifact.status_search_result: Theoretical few-body and optical-potential studies of η-³He near-threshold scattering have argued that Pauli blocking of πNN intermediate states substantially suppresses absorption, consistent with small empirical Im a(η³He). However, extractions of Im a(η³He) from data remain model-dependent and values nonzero in magnitude still appear in some analyses, so the question is best characterized as partially resolved rather than definitively closed.

status_evidence.title: Eta-mesic nuclei review
status_evidence.snippet: Pauli-principle blocking of the πNN intermediate state suppresses the most prominent inelastic channel in η-d and η-³He systems.
status_evidence.claim: The Pauli-blocking mechanism is the standard proposed explanation for the small Im a(η³He).
